subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- September 02, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - September 02, 2026

Hello, AcreetionOS community! Welcome to today's newsletter. Whether you are a long-time user or just discovering our Arch-based Linux distribution, we are glad to have you here. Our team continues to work diligently to bring you a stable, privacy-focused computing experience, and we have some exciting updates to share with you today.

In development news, Darren has been making important improvements to the Calamares installer configuration. The team fixed disk encryption handling to give users more flexibility, allowing them to add encryption during installation if desired rather than baking it into the default build. Additionally, gfxmode settings have been updated to prefer 1080p resolution over native 4K during boot, which should improve compatibility across a wider range of hardware configurations.

On the infrastructure side, the CI/CD pipelines are getting stronger with security enhancements. Natalie has been implementing Secret Detection and SAST (Static Application Security Testing) in the project workflows, helping catch potential vulnerabilities before they reach production. These improvements to our development processes reflect our commitment to building secure, reliable software.

The team has addressed a geocode-glib update conflict that could have affected installed systems. This fix ensures smoother package management for users who rely on location-based services, and we appreciate the community members who reported and helped diagnose the issue.

Firefox 155 was released recently, and if you have been following our rolling release model, you likely already have access to the latest features. This release includes notable improvements to privacy and performance that align well with our commitment to a telemetry-free experience. Remember that AcreetionOS pairs wonderfully with privacy-focused browsers like Fluorite, which is also developed by our team.

Security updates have been issued by major distributions this week, including patches from AlmaLinux and Debian for various packages. While AcreetionOS operates independently, our team monitors these disclosures to ensure our users are informed about potential vulnerabilities that might affect similar components. We recommend keeping your system updated through our repository to receive timely patches.

Here is a tip for today: if you are experiencing boot display issues, try adjusting your graphics settings in the BIOS or using the new gfxmode defaults that prefer 1080p. This can resolve blank screen problems on systems with older or less common graphics hardware.

Did you know that the Calamares installer used by AcreetionOS is customizable? Darren has been working on optimizing these configurations specifically for our distribution, meaning the installation experience is tailored to work seamlessly with our default settings while still giving advanced users the freedom to customize as needed.

For those interested in the technical side of our project, our GitLab instance at gitlab.acreetionos.org hosts all our repositories and CI/CD infrastructure. The addition of an MCP stdio server to our infrastructure tools represents our ongoing commitment to improving developer workflows and automation capabilities.

We want to hear from you! Join our Discord server at discord.acreetionos.org to connect with fellow community members, ask questions, and share your AcreetionOS experience. Thank you for being part of this journey as we continue building a user-friendly, privacy-focused Linux distribution together.
